h: The Summer Exhibition and other RA secrets
p: If there's one show the Royal Academy is famous for, it's the Summer Exhibition. It has run every single year since 1769, and the brilliant twist is that anyone can enter. Work by big-name Royal Academicians hangs right alongside pieces from first-timers, packed floor to ceiling in a riot of paintings, prints, sculpture and architecture. Plenty of the work is for sale, too, so you might spot something you fancy on your wall. It's busy, cheerful and nothing like a hushed, stuffy gallery.

Away from the ticketed shows, there are free displays from the RA's own collection to explore, plus the chance to see some real treasures. Keep an eye out for the Taddei Tondo, a marble relief by Michelangelo, which is a proper thrill to see up close. The building stretches right through from Piccadilly to Burlington Gardens, so take a wander through rather than heading straight back out the way you came.
How long to allow? A big exhibition can easily take a couple of hours if you read the labels and go back for a second look. Add time for the collection and a coffee, and half a day is about right.

Then step outside and make a proper afternoon of it. Burlington Arcade, the elegant Regency shopping arcade, runs right alongside. Fortnum and Mason is practically across the road for a nose at the hampers and posh teas, Piccadilly Circus is a short stroll east, and Green Park station is handy for heading home.
